title: Knowledge check: Preparing an API for Production

questions.prompt: Which practice belongs in a production-readiness checklist?
options: Commit production credentials into the frontend bundle for convenient deployment.
Use a single readiness log line as a substitute for monitoring and alerting.
Expose detailed exception traces to every API client.
Use external secret configuration, TLS, health signals, structured telemetry, and a documented recovery/rollback path.
questions.answer_key: Use external secret configuration, TLS, health signals, structured telemetry, and a documented recovery/rollback path.
questions.explanation: Use external secret configuration, TLS, health signals, structured telemetry, and a documented recovery/rollback path. This is especially relevant to “Preparing an API for Production” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Preparing an API for Production”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Verify deployment configuration, TLS, telemetry, alerting, health checks, and rollback.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
questions.answer_key: Verify deployment configuration, TLS, telemetry, alerting, health checks, and rollback.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Preparing an API for Production”?
options: The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
Secrets are committed, telemetry is missing, or rollback has not been planned.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
questions.answer_key: Secrets are committed, telemetry is missing, or rollback has not been planned.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
